extracted.intended_audience: graduate or advanced undergraduate students studying commutative algebra / algebraic geometry
extracted.subtask_description: Chapter/exercise notes on Noetherian rings, modules, and related algebraic geometry (Spec, constructible sets, going-down, primary decomposition, K-theory). Contains propositions, examples, and proofs used to recognize or construct Noetherian (or non-Noetherian) behavior and related module/ring properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: f_* preserves closedness (under going-up)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f has the going-up property then for primes qi in B with pi = f*(qi) we have V(pi) = f*(V(qi)); consequently f_* preserves closed sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument: use Exercise 5.10 i) (going-up) to compare V(pi) and images f*(V(qi)) and deduce closedness is preserved by f*.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ascending chains of prime ideals stabilize in Noetherian rings
rubrics_metrics.description: An ascending chain p1 ⊆ p2 ⊆ ··· of prime ideals induces a descending chain of closed sets V(p1) ⊇ V(p2) ⊇ ··· which stabilizes in a Noetherian topological space, hence the chain of prime ideals stabilizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to show the relationship between Noetherian property of Spec(A) and ACC on prime ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of finite generation (Claim XLVII)
rubrics_metrics.description: If B is a finitely generated A-algebra and C is a finitely generated B-module, then C is a finitely generated A-algebra.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof: express elements of C as finite A-polynomials in generators of B and generators of C as a B-module; then every element of C is a polynomial over A in those generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maximal non-finitely-generated ideal is prime (Zorn argument)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Σ is the set of ideals not finitely generated, then by Zorn’s lemma a maximal element p ∈ Σ exists, and such a maximal non-finitely-generated ideal must be prime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof by contradiction: if xy ∈ p but x,y ∉ p, show a+(x) or a+(y) would be finitely generated and lead to contradiction via (a:x) computations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization of Noetherian rings is Noetherian (examples via Hilbert basis theorem)
rubrics_metrics.description: If C is Noetherian then S^{-1}C[z] is Noetherian; in particular, rings obtained as localizations of polynomial rings (e.g., S^{-1}C[z] where S avoids a prime) are Noetherian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Hilbert Basis Theorem to get C[z] Noetherian and Proposition 7.3 to pass to localization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure of ideals in C[[z]] (principal ideals by order)
rubrics_metrics.description: In C[[z]] any ideal is of the form (z^k) for some k (or 0); (f) = (z^{ord(f)}) where ord(f) is the smallest index with nonzero coefficient. Hence C[[z]] is a PID, so Noetherian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use factorization f = z^{ord(f)}g with g a unit in C[[z]] to show principalness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example: subring of C[[z]] with bounded limsup is PID and Noetherian
rubrics_metrics.description: The subring A = {f ∈ C[[z]] : f = ∑ c_n z^n with lim sup_{n→∞} n-th_root(|c_n|) < ∞} inherits the principal ideal structure from C[[z]] and is Noetherian (PID).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show any f factors as z^m · g with g unit in C[[z]] and g lies in A, so ideals are (z^m) in A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counterexample: subring of C[[z]] with limsup = 0 is non-Noetherian
rubrics_metrics.description: The ring A = {f ∈ C[[z]] : lim sup_{n→∞} n-th_root(|c_n|) = 0} is not Noetherian: there exist functions f_n with (f_n) ⊂ (f_{n+1}) strictly, giving an infinite ascending chain of ideals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct a sequence f_n with radii of convergence tending in a way that f_{n+1} divides f_n inside the big ring but not vice versa within A, producing a strictly increasing chain of ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite generation via module-finite extension (example C + (z^{k+1})C[z])
rubrics_metrics.description: Rings of the form A = C + (z^{k+1})C[z] are Noetherian because they are finitely generated modules over a Noetherian subring (C[z^{k+1}]) and hence finitely generated algebras.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show A is a module generated by {1, z, ..., z^k} over C[z^{k+1}] and apply Proposition 7.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example: subring defined by vanishing derivatives (non-Noetherian)
rubrics_metrics.description: The ring A = {f(z,w) ∈ C[z,w] : ∂^n/∂w^n|_{z=0} f = 0 for all n} equals C[z] + zC[w] and is not Noetherian: the chain of ideals (zw) ⊂ (zw, zw^2) ⊂ ··· is strictly increasing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute the explicit description A = C[z] + (z)C[w] and produce the infinite ascending chain of ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrality and finite generation imply finite generation of subalgebra (application of Prop.7.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: If B is integral over BG and B is a finitely generated A-algebra with A Noetherian, then certain intermediate subrings (like B0) are finitely generated A-algebras (apply Proposition 7.8).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use integrality properties and finite generation transitivity between A, BG, and B to apply Proposition 7.8.

rubrics_metrics.name: No finitely generated field extension of Z in characteristic 0 (finitely generated fields over Z lead to contradiction)
rubrics_metrics.description: If K is a field of characteristic 0 and is finitely generated as a Z-algebra, this leads to a contradiction (since it would force Q to be finitely generated as a Z-algebra); in characteristic p, a finitely generated algebraic field is finite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use that Z→K injects, so Q ⊂ K; finite generation forces K finite algebraic over Q (impossible as Q is not finitely generated over Z), whereas in char p one gets a finite field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hilbert basis corollary for polynomial rings
rubrics_metrics.description: k[t1,...,tn] is Noetherian; an ideal generated by an indexed family {f_α}_{α∈I} is finitely generated because some finite subset of the family generates the same ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Corollary 7.6 (Hilbert Basis Theorem) to reduce infinite generating families to finite generators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polynomial ring in one variable: Noetherianity passes to coefficient ring
rubrics_metrics.description: If A[x] is Noetherian then A is Noetherian (since A ≅ A[x]/(x)), so Noetherianity descends from polynomial ring modulo principal ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use A[x]/(x) ≅ A and Proposition 6.6 on images of Noetherian rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finite generation of an ideal from its localizations at maximal ideals
rubrics_metrics.description: If an ideal a ⊂ A has the property that its extension in each localization A_m (for maximal ideals m containing a) is finitely generated, then a itself is finitely generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct a finite set of elements from these local generators whose generated ideal a0 has the same localization at each maximal ideal; by Proposition 3.9 conclude a0=a.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noetherian behaviour of modules and polynomial extensions (M[x])
rubrics_metrics.description: If M and A[x] are Noetherian (e.g., by Hilbert basis theorem for A[x]) and M[x] ≅ M_A ⊕ A[x] yields exact sequences showing M_A[x] is Noetherian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use exact sequence 0→ker→M⊕A[x]→M_A[x]→0 and Proposition 6.3 to deduce Noetherianity from finite generation of source.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization at primes can be Noetherian even if ring is not
rubrics_metrics.description: For A = ∏_{n∈N} Z/2Z (non-Noetherian), for any prime p the localization A_p is actually a field (hence Noetherian).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show pA_p = 0 and that nonzero elements become invertible in the localization, producing a field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contraction injectivity and Noetherianity (descent)
rubrics_metrics.description: If for every ideal a of A the map a ↦ a·e (extension followed by contraction) is injective and B is Noetherian, then A is Noetherian (ascending chains in A map injectively to ascending chains in B which stabilize).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Exercise 3.16 i) and injectivity to pull back stabilization from B to A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fibers of morphism and Noetherianity of fibers (finite type case)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a finite type morphism f: A→B and p∈Spec(A), the fiber f*^{-1}(p) ≅ Spec(B_p/pB_p) = Spec(k(p)⊗_A B) is Noetherian (since B_p/pB_p is a finitely generated algebra over a field).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use that B is a finitely generated A-algebra, B_p is Noetherian and Proposition 6.6 to deduce Noetherianity of quotient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Radical vs vanishing ideal relationship (Nullstellensatz-style argument)
rubrics_metrics.description: For finitely generated k-algebra A and ideal a, r(a) ⊆ I(V(a)); conversely if f ∈ r(a) then use reductions to quotient and maximal ideals to show f vanishes on V(a), giving the equality in the appropriate context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use passage to B=A/p, localization B_f, maximal ideals m in C=B_f and evaluation to algebraically closed fields to deduce vanishing/equality statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent conditions for flatness/free finite modules over local rings
rubrics_metrics.description: For a finitely generated module M over a local ring A the conditions: (i) M is flat, (ii) M is free, (iii) Tor_1^A(A/m, M)=0 and generation conditions on M/mM are equivalent, culminating in M being free if these hold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Nakayama's lemma, exact sequences, and dimension counts over A/m to pass between free, flat, and Tor vanishing conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Localization preserves freeness for finitely generated flat modules
rubrics_metrics.description: If M is a finitely generated flat A-module then for any prime p the localization M_p is a free A_p-module (Ap is local Noetherian, Mp stays finitely generated and flat).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Corollary 7.4 and Exercise 7.15 to infer freeness at localizations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Noetherian module: decomposition into irreducible modules
rubrics_metrics.description: In a Noetherian module every submodule is a finite intersection of irreducible submodules (Lemma 7.11-1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses Zorn’s lemma on non-decomposable submodules and maximality to force finite intersection decomposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irreducible submodule in Noetherian module is primary
rubrics_metrics.description: In a Noetherian module every irreducible submodule is primary: passing to quotient it suffices to show 0 irreducible implies 0 primary and deduce nilpotence of zero divisors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ascending chain of annihilators Ann_M(x^n) and ACC to find n with Ann(x^n)=Ann(x^{n+1}) and conclude primaryness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary decomposition and associated primes (existence and equivalences)
rubrics_metrics.description: If 0 has a primary decomposition in a Noetherian module M then each prime associated to 0 arises as Ann(x) for some x∈M and there exist submodules isomorphic to A/p inside M; conversely such submodules produce associated primes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use irredundant primary decomposition, Proposition 7.14, and properties of annihilators to connect primary components with annihilators of elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniqueness of minimal primary decomposition radicals
rubrics_metrics.description: Given two minimal primary decompositions N = ⋂_{i=1}^r B_i = ⋂_{j=1}^s C_j of a submodule, one has r=s and after renumbering r_M(B_i)=r_M(C_i) for all i (radicals of components coincide).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the hint involving projections and irreducibility of zero in quotient modules to compare components and deduce equality of number and radicals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Constructible sets in Noetherian spaces: form and properties
rubrics_metrics.description: The Boolean algebra F generated by open sets equals finite unions of sets of the form U∩C where U is open and C closed; such constructible sets behave well under finite unions/intersections and finite complements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show finite unions of U∩C can be re-expressed as a single U∩C and use closure properties of F to deduce membership tests and density/open criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: constructible set contains nonempty open subset iff dense in irreducible closed component
rubrics_metrics.description: If E is constructible and meets an irreducible closed component X0 then E∩X0 is either empty or contains a nonempty open subset of X0; conversely density of E∩X0 forces it to contain a nonempty open subset (Exercise 7.21/7.20).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use representation E=U∩C and minimality/irreducibility arguments to translate density into containing nonempty open subsets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image of constructible sets under finite-type morphisms is constructible
rubrics_metrics.description: If f: Spec(B)→Spec(A) is of finite type and E ⊂ Spec(B) is constructible, then f*(E) is constructible in Spec(A).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce to E open in Y and cover by finitely many basic opens Spec(B_g); then analyze images on irreducible components using injectivity reductions and use algebraically closed field extensions to produce preimages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Going-down property ↔ f* is open (for finite type maps)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f has the going-down property then f* is open; conversely, if f* is open then f has going-down. In particular, going-down implies f*(Y) is open for basic opens Y_g.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the behavior of chains of primes and images of basic opens together with density criteria for irreducible components to translate going-down into openness and vice versa (Exercises 5.10, 7.22–7.24).

rubrics_metrics.name: K-theory: definition and generators of K(A)
rubrics_metrics.description: K(A) is defined as C(A)/D(A) where C(A) is free abelian group on isomorphism classes of finitely generated modules and D(A) relations from short exact sequences; K(A) is generated by γ(A/p) for prime ideals p (from composition series).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Jordan–Hölder style chains of modules with factors ≅ A/p to express any class in K(A) as sum of γ(A/p)'s.

rubrics_metrics.name: K(A) for PID: infinite cyclic generated by γ(A)
rubrics_metrics.description: If A is a PID then for any nonzero principal ideal (a) we have γ(A/(a))=0 in K(A), so K(A) is an infinite cyclic group generated by γ(A) (coming from A/(0)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use short exact sequences 0→A→A→A/(a)→0 given by multiplication by a to show γ(A/(a)) vanishes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functoriality and module/ring structures on K-theory
rubrics_metrics.description: F1(A) with tensor product is a commutative ring, D1(A) an ideal, and K1(A)=F1(A)/D1(A) a commutative ring. K(A) is a K1(A)-module via tensor product; finite ring maps f: A→B induce maps f! on K-theory satisfying functoriality (composition) and module-homomorphism properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prove tensor product respects exact sequences and passes to quotients; construct f! via tensoring with B and apply universal properties; verify (h∘f)! = h!∘f!.
